<<DEMONPC0 [00 00 FF]>>The bagworm <<PAUSE [08]>>is not a worm
per se, but rather any moth
of the family Psychidae while
in its caterpillar phase.<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>>Bagworms construct their
cocoons by cutting leaves or
branches to the length of<<PAUSE [08]>>
their own bodies.<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>>Next, <<PAUSE [04]>>they hang these leaves
or branches on shrubs or
trees and spin their cocoons
around them.<<PAUSE [06]>> Fascinating!<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>>Interestingly enough, <<PAUSE [04]>>only
males of the species become
moths. <<PAUSE [08]>>Females spend the rest
of their lives in the cocoons.<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>>The black, furry males fly
from cocoon to cocoon,<<PAUSE [04]>>
leaving the females to lay
500 or so eggs, then die.<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>>Just imagine it! <<PAUSE [04]>>500 or more
eggs!<<PAUSE [04]>> And then they die!<<PAUSE [04]>>
That's not very sporting,
if you ask me. <<PAUSE [04]>>Not at all!<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>><<DEMONPC0 [00 00 15]>>I can't see any female owls
standing for that nonsense.<<PAUSE [04]>>
My dear old mum would have
given my da an earful, wot!<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>><<DEMONPC0 [00 00 FF]>>In any case, where was I?<<PAUSE [08]>>
Ah, yes.<<PAUSE [07]>> Bagworms, bagworms.<<PAUSE [06]>>
Quite the pests, they are...<<PAUSE [04]>>
Voracious in the extreme!<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>>An infestation of bagworms
can defoliate entire trees
in surprisingly rapid fashion.<<PAUSE [08]>>
Gluttonous monsters!<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>><<DEMONPC0 [00 00 16]>>This is particularly harmful,
sometimes fatally so,
in evergreens, <<PAUSE [06]>>whose needles
are never replaced.<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>><<DEMONPC0 [00 00 FF]>>Hundreds and hundreds of
bagworms...<<PAUSE [08]>><<DEMONPC0 [00 00 17]>>eating and eating...<<PAUSE [08]>>
stuffing their bug-gullets...<<PAUSE [08]>>
<<DEMONPC0 [00 00 16]>>Bleeech! <<PAUSE [06]>>Wretched villains!<<BTN>>
<<MSGCLEAR>><<DEMONPC0 [00 00 FF]>>Hooo...<<PAUSE [08]>> But I digress...<<PAUSE [08]>>
<<MSGCONTINUE>>
